excerpt: Representative fMRI and neuroimaging pictures do not convey the complex biological and computational steps that lead to inferences about brain structure and function; group averages, cross-sectional designs, head movement, cardiorespiratory effects, and the vein-drain problem can create artifacts or limit causal interpretation.
overview: This formal methodological argument explains why striking brain images should not be translated directly into clinical or practical recommendations. The source accepts that meta-analyses suggest modest brain changes, but stresses that artifacts, comparators, causality, and practical significance remain unresolved.
title: Neuroimaging Confound Chain
